data.text: Bramber Software Limited  |  Legal & Commercial  |  Version 3.1  |  Owner: Aisha Bello, Commercial Counsel  |  Reviewed 9 January 2026
Use this matrix for mutual and one-way NDAs. Start with the definition and purpose rows; record every deviation and route it to the approver named in the row.

Information disclosed in any form that is marked confidential, or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential from its nature and the circumstances of disclosure. The definition should be symmetrical for a mutual NDA.
A broad definition covering oral, written and electronic information, provided it is limited to information disclosed for the Purpose and excludes information already in the public domain.
A definition that captures information independently developed by the recipient, information received without a duty of confidence, or the recipient's own pre-existing know-how.
Watch for 'all information disclosed by either party' with no purpose limitation. It reads broad but is unworkable and usually signals a template copied from a different deal.

Use is limited to evaluating a potential commercial relationship between the parties. The purpose should be described in one sentence and should not include 'any business purpose' or 'the parties' ongoing relationship'.
A purpose that covers evaluation, negotiation and, for a mutual NDA, the performance of a pilot or proof of concept for up to 90 days.
A purpose that permits use for product development, benchmarking, training AI models, or any purpose unrelated to the disclosed opportunity.
If the counterparty wants to include a pilot, add the pilot scope and a fixed end date. Do not rely on 'evaluation' to cover production use.

Written information should be marked confidential at the time of disclosure. Oral information is confidential if identified as confidential at disclosure and confirmed in writing within 10 Business Days.
No marking requirement for written information, provided the definition is limited to information a reasonable person would treat as confidential.
A requirement that Bramber mark every document, slide or email, or a rule that unmarked information loses protection entirely.
A strict marking regime is an administrative trap for the sales team. Prefer the reasonable-person standard.

Disclosure is permitted to directors, employees, professional advisers and contractors who need to know the information for the Purpose and who are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as protective as the NDA. The disclosing party remains responsible for its representatives.
Disclosure to affiliates and bona fide prospective investors or acquirers, subject to a written confidentiality undertaking and notice to the discloser.
Disclosure to 'any third party' or to representatives without a need-to-know or without a confidentiality obligation.
Investors are a common ask in fundraising. A named list plus a written undertaking is usually enough.

Standard exclusions: information already public without breach; information lawfully received from a third party without a duty of confidence; information independently developed without use of the confidential information; information known to the recipient before disclosure; and disclosure required by law or a regulator, subject to notice where lawful.
The standard exclusions, plus a narrow carve-out for information approved for release in writing by the discloser.
An NDA with no exclusions, or one that excludes only public information and omits independently developed information and compelled disclosure.
The compelled-disclosure carve-out is non-negotiable. Regulators do not wait for a counterparty's consent.
The NDA runs for 2 years from the effective date, and confidentiality obligations survive for 3 years from disclosure. Trade secrets may be protected for as long as they remain trade secrets.
A 3-year term with 3-year survival. A 5-year term, or a 5-year survival, only for genuinely sensitive information and with GC approval.
Perpetual confidentiality for all information, a term of more than 5 years, or an indefinite survival period with no trade-secret carve-out.
Aisha Bello; Priya Raghavan for any 5-year term or anything beyond 5 years
Most inbound NDAs say 5 years. A 5-year term is not our default; it needs GC approval under NDA-06 and should be recorded as a concession.

On written request or termination, the recipient returns or destroys confidential information, including copies, and certifies destruction on request. One copy may be retained for legal or regulatory compliance, subject to continuing confidentiality.
Destruction within 30 days of request, with a certification signed by an authorised officer; retention of backup copies for a defined period.
An obligation to destroy backups immediately, or a right for the discloser to enter the recipient's premises to verify destruction.
Backups are a technical reality. A 30-day destruction window and a retention carve-out for archives are standard.
No residuals clause. The recipient may use general knowledge, skills and experience retained in unaided memory, but not any document, model, dataset or intentionally memorised information.
A narrow residuals clause limited to unaided memory, with an express exclusion for intentionally memorised information and any use that would infringe IP.
A residuals clause that permits use of confidential information for product development, benchmarking or AI training, or that applies to trade secrets.
Residuals clauses are common in US templates. They are acceptable only if the carve-out is narrow and the information is not used to compete.
No non-solicitation in an NDA unless it is mutual, limited to employees directly involved in the opportunity, and lasts no more than 12 months. General recruitment advertising is excluded.
A mutual 12-month non-solicitation with a general-advertising carve-out and a carve-out for employees who approach the recipient unsolicited.
A one-way non-solicit, a non-hire provision, a term longer than 12 months, or a restriction that covers all employees of the counterparty group.
Aisha Bello; Priya Raghavan for any non-hire
A non-solicit is a restraint of trade. Keep it narrow or take it out; it rarely survives a dispute and it slows down recruitment.

The parties acknowledge that damages may be inadequate and that injunctive relief is available, without the need to prove actual loss or post a bond. This is mutual and does not create an admission of liability.
Injunctive relief subject to the court's discretion, with a requirement to notify the other party before applying except where notice would defeat the purpose.
Liquidated damages, a pre-agreed damages figure, or an admission of irreparable harm that binds Bramber in a later dispute.
Courts grant injunctions on their own terms. The clause is a signal, not a guarantee.
English law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.
Delaware or New York law for US counterparties, with courts in the counterparty's state; German law for German counterparties where the NDA is ancillary to a German-law MSA.
Arbitration in a jurisdiction where Bramber has no presence, a foreign court with no connection to either party, or a clause that requires disputes to be heard in more than one forum.
Aisha Bello; Priya Raghavan for any non-English law
NDAs are low-value, high-volume documents. Do not spend billable time on jurisdiction unless there is a real dispute risk.
No public announcement or use of the other party's name or logo without prior written consent. The NDA itself is confidential.
A factual statement that the parties are in discussions, agreed in writing in advance; a tombstone announcement after signing.
A right for the counterparty to announce the relationship or use Bramber's logo without approval, or a press release that describes the commercial terms.
Marketing often asks for a logo before the NDA is signed. The answer is no until the NDA is executed.

This workbook is the working position for mutual and one-way NDAs signed by Bramber Software Limited. It is maintained by Commercial Legal and used by Sales, Partnerships and Legal Operations.
Owner: Aisha Bello, Commercial Counsel. Version 3.1, reviewed 9 January 2026. Next review: January 2027.

Start with the Definition and Purpose rows. If either is outside our position, the rest of the NDA is usually not worth negotiating until it is fixed. Then check Term and Exclusions. Record every deviation in the deal summary and route it to the approver named in the row.
Use the Bramber mutual NDA template for sales conversations and the one-way NDA template where Bramber is the discloser. Counterparty paper is acceptable if the matrix positions are met.

Where Bramber is the recipient, the same positions apply but the obligations are one-sided. Do not accept a one-way NDA where Bramber is the discloser unless the counterparty has a genuine need to receive information and the scope is limited.

Aisha Bello approves all NDA deviations. Priya Raghavan approves any term beyond 5 years, any non-hire provision, and any governing law other than England and Wales, Delaware or New York. Nadia Iqbal is consulted on publicity.

Five-year terms, residuals clauses, non-solicitation, and disclosure to investors. Each has a documented fallback in the matrix. If a counterparty asks for all four at once, escalate rather than trading them.
Send the draft, the counterparty name, the deal context and the specific rows in issue to the Legal Operations desk. Do not send a redline without the row references.

3.1 (9 Jan 2026): added AI-training restriction to NDA-02 and NDA-08; refreshed investor disclosure position. 3.0 (14 Apr 2025): converted from Word to this workbook. 2.4 (2 Sep 2024): added non-solicitation guidance.
Terms beyond 5 years, non-hire, non-English law.
